classification_is_not_deterministic.statement: Repeated executions over an IDENTICAL package agree on substance but NOT on severity classification. This is a measured property of the review, not a defect to be tuned out, and it is recorded here so a later session cannot rediscover it as a surprise.
classification_is_not_deterministic.evidence: Two live passes over the byte-identical P1_V4 package on claude-opus-5, 2026-08-17: req_011Ce7vK9W58YKue3dLAnZuj returned 1 MAJOR (the absent-reference problem raised as a finding); req_011Ce7vY2dBsvNN3iaBqWjZW returned 0 findings, classifying every reference-dependent category as UNCERTAIN_MISSING_EVIDENCE instead. Both are ledgered in rbv4_call_budget.json. The dispositions agreed on what was seen; only the severity assignment moved.
classification_is_not_deterministic.consequence_for_consumers: A finding COUNT is not a measurement and must never be a gate input. RBV-5 binds to specific dispositions or to nothing; real_bottle_visual_comparison/1.0 takes review findings as EVIDENCE only, which is also what §R1d requires.
classification_is_not_deterministic.what_would_change_this: A stability characterisation across N repeated passes with the count distribution recorded — not yet run, and it would spend owner-budgeted calls.
